clue.text: Object to church youth leader, being unable to relax

parts.note: it is the pronoun standing for any object or thing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of youth is used

explanation.surface: A youth worker objects to the church because the young people cannot settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and fidgety, longing to get going, is described as itchy.

clue.text: Oscar fixed repeat function

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of repaired or rearranged, telling us to rework the letters of repeat

explanation.surface: Oscar has mended a function on a machine that repeats things.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to work it, so both words mean to run or perform.

clue.text: Social worker with quarter stake

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a social insect colony
E for east is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A social worker puts up a quarter of the money as a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a council employee but is the insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Clergyman's has a trick after card he played

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the rearranged letters
played in the sense of performed or tampered with, signalling that card and he are rearranged

parts.note: a con is a confidence trick, a swindle

explanation.surface: A clergyman is said to be up to a trick after a card game he played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' turns CARD HE into ARCHDE; 'after' puts A and CON (trick) behind it. The 's of 'Clergyman's' stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Clergyman is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Anglican cleric ranking below a bishop, responsible for part of a diocese.

clue.text: Captain initially going east for fish

indicators.note: in an across answer east is the right-hand end, so the opening letter travels there

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a ship or team

explanation.surface: The captain heads east at first, off to find fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially going east' takes the S at the start of SKIPPER and moves it to the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoked split herrings, a traditional British breakfast dish, are kippers.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about promoting new joint

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down answer the letter for new is moved higher

parts.note: keen on or about something means enthusiastic about it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to see a new joint venture launched.
explanation.walkthrough: In KEEN, 'promoting' lifts the N (new) to sit second, giving KNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge in the leg between thigh and shin.

clue.text: Caller had a long time in public relations

indicators.note: in puts the long time inside the letters for public relations

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone who phoned had to wait ages for the public relations office.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager or bleeper alerts its carrier that someone wants them, so it calls them.

clue.text: One moved by danger

parts.note: reads as someone emotionally stirred by peril, but means a person relocated from a dangerous area, as children were in wartime

explanation.surface: A person deeply affected by peril.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime child sent from the cities to the countryside to escape bombing.

clue.text: Woolly protectors

parts.note: suggests thick knitwear or vague guardians, but means those who guard woolly animals in the field

explanation.surface: Knitted garments that keep you safe from the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who tend and guard flocks of sheep, the woolly animals.

clue.text: Dinar/punt exchange is hardly cricket!

indicators.note: exchange fits the currency surface and tells us to swap the letters about

explanation.surface: Swapping dinars for punts in a currency deal is not quite proper conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges DINAR PUNT. A dinar and a punt are currencies; 'not cricket' means unsporting, but here the phrase is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip and run is an informal knockabout version of the game where batters must run whenever they hit the ball, so barely the real sport.

clue.text: Serious points at first impress deeply

indicators.note: at first places the compass points at the front, before the word for serious

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
grave means serious or solemn

explanation.surface: Serious points made early on leave a deep impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut lettering into a surface, figuratively to fix firmly in the mind.

clue.text: Plate rumoured to be very "you", luckily

annotationWithheld.why: Plate rumoured to be very "you", luckily (9) gives HORSESHOE; the homophone cannot be resolved: no reading of 'very you' sounds like the answer, and no blog parse was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Plate rumoured to be very "you", luckily

clue.text: Trading capital and violent depression

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening capital letter, so the start of Trading is used

parts.note: rough means violent, as in rough treatment

explanation.surface: A trading city sinks into a violent slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trading capital' looks like a financial centre but is just the first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: In weather a trough is an elongated area of low pressure; more generally a low point or dip.

clue.text: Squeeze on the media

explanation.surface: Putting pressure on journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to squeeze; the press is the newspapers and journalists collectively.

clue.text: Charge up devouring energy fruit

indicators.note: devouring means eating, so one piece swallows the letter for energy
in a down answer up means read the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in taking the rap
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A fee hike eats up energy supplies before the fruit harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP into PAR, and 'devouring' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet, juicy tree fruit narrowing towards the stalk.

clue.text: Vehicles that show the marks of battle

parts.note: to sport is to show off or wear something, as in sporting a tie
scars are marks left by wounds, as from fighting

explanation.surface: Battered cars that display the damage from fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Low fast two-seater cars built for speed and handling are the motoring type meant.

clue.text: Flyer protected by Tuareg rebels

indicators.note: protected by suggests the bird is enclosed and sheltered within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pilot is guarded by desert rebels of the Sahara.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sits within 'TuaREG REBels'; the Tuareg are nomads of the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving water bird, and birds are the crossword's usual flyers.

clue.text: Fighter hears primate

indicators.note: hears tells us the next word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a gorilla is the largest of the primates

explanation.surface: A soldier listens out for a great ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an irregular force waging small-scale war against regular troops.

clue.text: Develop a marine platform to cover unit

indicators.note: to cover means to go round, so the platform encloses the word for unit

parts.note: a pier is a platform running out into the sea
one is the unit number

explanation.surface: Build a seaside platform to shelter a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to be first to devise or open up something new, so to originate it.

clue.text: It's regularly your fault for using speech

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one of your fault

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed, and it is their fault for talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'yOuR fAuLt' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes anything done by mouth, spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Blimey! Chef's nearly finished

indicators.note: nearly finished means the word stops just short of its end, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a cook is a chef

explanation.surface: Gosh, the chef is almost done with the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Chef's' is a link meaning 'is'; COOK loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is a dated British exclamation of surprise, like gosh or crikey.

clue.text: I welcome motorway pub stop

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the self holds the motorway and pub inside

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone happy to see a pub at a motorway service stop.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade, that halts it.

clue.text: Title given to circle in London district

indicators.note: in places the circle inside the London district

parts.note: Barnet is a borough of north London
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A peerage awarded to a ring of people in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is a borough on London's northern edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary rank below a baron, styled Sir.

clue.text: A season back in the mountains of Africa

indicators.note: back says the word for season is read in reverse

parts.note: to season food is to salt it

explanation.surface: A season spent back among the mountains of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SALT into TLAS. 'season' is a verb (to flavour), not a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas is the range running across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Miss Seoul to be modelled

indicators.note: be modelled means be shaped anew, telling us to rearrange the letters of Seoul to

explanation.surface: A beauty queen from Seoul is about to pose for a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be modelled' rearranges SEOUL TO. 'Miss' looks like a beauty title but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose out is to fail to get something, which is what missing a chance means.

clue.text: Place of birth?

parts.note: reads as a birthplace generally, but points to a South African province whose name also means relating to birth

explanation.surface: A form asks where someone was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal, now KwaZulu-Natal, is a South African province; the word also means connected with birth.

clue.text: Gunners take a breather — that's most unusual

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
to rest is to take a breather

explanation.surface: Artillerymen pausing for a break is a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' points to the Royal Artillery, not to Arsenal football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, meaning least common.

clue.text: Act in part with a display of temper

explanation.surface: A performer flies into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a division within an act of a play; making a scene is a public tantrum.

clue.text: Way that's always direct

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A road that is always straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direct' looks like an adjective meaning straight but is the verb, to guide.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or point something on its course.

clue.text: At home, Mr Attlee was not very nice

parts.note: in means at home
Clement Attlee was British Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: Gossip that the post-war prime minister was unpleasant in private.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee led Britain's post-war Labour government.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement usually describes harsh, stormy weather, an unpleasant state.

clue.text: Very keen on it, perhaps?

parts.note: an enthusiast is said to be well ... something, and ... it is the phrase the question hints at

explanation.surface: Someone who seems enthusiastic about a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, being into a hobby means being very enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Let out when prison term is up

indicators.note: in a down answer is up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: doing time means serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A convict released once the sentence has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns TIME round in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or release, such as heat or a sound.

clue.text: Light shows queen bearing on student worker

indicators.note: on places the queen and bearing after the student and worker in an across answer

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, the usual crossword student
an ant is a worker insect
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Lights show the queen keeping watch over a student labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a protective case.

clue.text: In France you put ride off — for depravity!

parts.note: tu is French for you

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or awry, so the letters of put ride are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French speaker cancelling a ride, calling it wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: TU is the French for 'you' used between friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is moral baseness or wickedness, as in moral turpitude.

clue.text: Style of design company poorly rated initially

indicators.note: initially puts the rearranged letters first, ahead of the company
poorly means badly, so the letters of rated are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A design firm that was badly reviewed from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the bold geometric decorative fashion of the 1920s and 1930s.
